title: user.decision_policy — Decision Policy Pack Record
description: Schema for a single record in the user.decision_policy pack (#5 of 14): how the subject decides — priority orderings, tradeoff resolutions, conditions under which an action is approved or rejected, and thresholds that force escalation to a human (DecisionPolicy node). Each record extends the unified base record via allOf $ref to ./record.base.schema.json and narrows record_type to this pack's five types. Routed from DecisionPolicyCandidate (see ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6 routing); attached to the subject by the `prioritizes` edge and to rejection conditions by the `rejects_when` edge (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §4). Feeds the rejection_alignment / decision_fidelity evaluation metrics. Pack definition: ../spec/03-pack-catalog.md (user.decision_policy); base record: ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §7.

record_type.description: Decision-policy record kind. PriorityRuleRecord: a fixed ordering the subject applies when goals compete (e.g. 'correctness before speed'). TradeoffRuleRecord: how to resolve a specific tension between two desirable things, including the acceptable cost (e.g. 'trade scope for a firm deadline, never quality'). ApprovalConditionRecord: the conditions under which the subject is willing to approve/go ahead with an action. RejectionRuleRecord: conditions under which the subject refuses or backs out (pairs with the `rejects_when` edge and user.red_flags). EscalationThresholdRecord: a measurable threshold past which the agent must hand the decision back to the human (ties to base sensitivity and user.boundary_authority ask_confirm).

decision_axis.description: Short label for the dimension this policy governs (e.g. 'quality_vs_speed', 'cost_vs_thoroughness', 'autonomy', 'irreversibility'). Clusters related decision records without inventing per-record vocabulary; display detail over the canonical base `statement`.

priority_order.description: For PriorityRuleRecord: the competing factors listed most-important-first (e.g. ['correctness', 'clarity', 'speed', 'brevity']). Refines `statement` into an ordering an evaluator (decision_fidelity) can score directly.

tradeoff.description: For TradeoffRuleRecord: the structured tension and its resolution. Optional convenience over `statement`.

give_up.description: What the subject is willing to sacrifice.

to_protect.description: What must be preserved in exchange.

acceptable_cost.description: The limit of the concession (e.g. 'up to one extra day, never a quality regression').

approve_when.description: For ApprovalConditionRecord: conjunctive conditions that must hold for the subject to approve the action (e.g. ['evidence_refs ≥ 2', 'reversible', 'inside confirmed scope']). All must be true unless an exception_rules clause says otherwise.

reject_when.description: For RejectionRuleRecord: conditions that trigger refusal or back-out (e.g. ['external comms without confirm', 'no supporting evidence', 'identity-sensitive claim']). Mirrors the `rejects_when` edge; feeds rejection_alignment scoring.

escalation_threshold.description: For EscalationThresholdRecord: the measurable trigger that forces ask_confirm / hand-back to the human. Optional structured form of `statement`.

comparator.description: Comparison operator against the threshold value.

value.description: Threshold value (string to allow units/currency, e.g. '$500', '0.7', '3 people').

escalate_to.description: Authority action taken when the threshold is crossed; aligns with the boundary authority ladder (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md, user.boundary_authority).

default_action.description: What the agent should do at runtime when this policy is the matching, runtime-active rule and its conditions are met. Conservative by design; never overrides a stricter BoundaryRule.

applies_to_decisions.description: Decision kinds/contexts where this policy is in effect (e.g. ['merging a PR', 'sending an external email', 'choosing scope cuts']). Narrows the required base `scope` without weakening it (Gate G2); complements base linked_projects/linked_domains.

conflicts_with.description: Other decision_policy record ids this rule can collide with at runtime. Conflicts resolve via review and priority_weight, not silently; does not bypass review_status gates.

$comment: Required fields are inherited unchanged from record.base.schema.json (id, record_type, label, statement, evidence_refs, confidence, scope, review_status, sensitivity, created_at, updated_at). All fields added here are OPTIONAL — required = base required only, per the pack-focus rule. Base validation still applies: evidence_refs ≥ 1 (G1), non-empty scope (G2), counterexamples required when confidence < 0.7, exception_rules required when sensitivity ∈ {sensitive, restricted}. Display aliases for `statement`: 'rule_statement'/'decision_rule' may be shown in UIs but the stored field is `statement` (구 코드명 pa.t05).
